baseline: 9bf7d80 implementations of ascii probes. Prior transaction guard and MERGE changes retained.
platform: Windows x64; Rust 1.93.0 bench (fat LTO); Dart 3.14.0 AOT
commands: from native: cargo bench -p odbc_engine --bench cell_reader_bench -- "wide_text_to_utf8/(original_ascii_cell|ascii_fast_cell)" --sample-size 30 --warm-up-time 1 --measurement-time 1 --noplot
dart compile exe benchmarks/large_result_live.dart -o .tmp/large-live.exe; run twice with ODBC_FAST_NATIVE_LIBRARY pointing at the tested release DLL
notes: Rust compares original and current cell conversion for identical ASCII payloads in one optimized executable, 30 Criterion samples.
Dart uses 10 warmup pairs then 31 alternating pairs. Keys encode byte length, high-bit position (-1 = all ASCII), and original (true) vs candidate (false).
Read-only SQL Server fixture: 512 ordered rows, 2 integers; optional NVARCHAR(MAX) with 2048 ASCII characters, NULL every seventh row. Four warmups then 21 samples per workload per run.

Direct uses Windows PowerShell with System.Data.Odbc. FFI includes the Dart binding and transfer of the wire buffer. Public Dart API uses balancedServer; columnar result converted to rows for validation after the API timer stops. checked includes value verification; direct times include reading all values into arrays. Direct first row is measured just after the first successful Read. Connections opened outside timing.
Live timings compare paths on the final build, not old vs new. Driver binding, buffering and materialization differ. No attribution of the differences to a single layer.
